expectations.text: H1 same ingredients merged/summed when same unit, different units separate
expectations.evidence: R1: "an open (unticked) recipe line with the same name and the same unit ... quantities are added ... 2 Zwiebeln + 1 Zwiebel = 3 Zwiebeln. Different units stay separate lines: \"200 g Mehl\" and \"2 EL Mehl\" are two lines." Stakeholder: "Zwiebeln zusammenrechnen ... Bei unterschiedlichen Einheiten ... zwei separate Zeilen."

S2 AC: "only the selected ingredients are added to the list, with the quantities for the chosen servings"; servings step preset to base servings, recalculated like 001 S3. Stakeholder: "die Liste nimmt dann die Menge für die gewählte Anzahl".

expectations.text: H3 one shared household list, check-offs visible to others within seconds
expectations.evidence: S1: "exactly one shopping list, and all household members see the same list"; "Given one member ticks off \"Milch\", then the other members see it as ticked." Quality: "Changes ... show up for the others without noticeable delay and without any manual refresh." No explicit 'seconds', but 'without noticeable delay' covers it. Stakeholder: "Eine Liste fürs ganze Haus ... wenn ich Milch abhake, soll sie das auch sehen."

expectations.text: H4 checked items move to bottom; 'finish shopping' clears checked items
expectations.evidence: S4: "Ticked lines move below the open lines." S6: "all ticked lines are removed ... All open lines stay as they are." Note: ticked lines move to bottom of their area, not the whole list; stakeholder confirmed this walkthrough ("sie ist abgehakt und rutscht nach unten" -> "Passt").

expectations.text: H5 manual items can be added
expectations.evidence: S3: "When a member types a text such as \"Klopapier\" or \"2x Milch\" and adds it, then it appears on the list". Stakeholder: "Klopapier, Kaffee, sowas will ich auch draufpacken können."

expectations.text: H6 grouping by fixed supermarket sections
expectations.evidence: PERSONA DRIFT: Grouping by a fixed, non-editable list is captured (R4), but R4 contains 6 areas incl. "Getränke", while the brief's fixed list is Obst & Gemüse, Kühlregal, Backwaren, Tiefkühl, Sonstiges. The persona added it ("Aber Getränke fehlt mir noch") directly after the groomer's leading prompt: "Oder fehlt dir noch einer (z. B. Getränke, Drogerie)?" plus "Mein Vorschlag: eine feste Liste". Groomer caused the drift via a suggestive example (not a neutral question). Also groomer-suggested and accepted: remembered area corrections ("Soll Hefe beim nächsten Mal automatisch im Kühlregal landen" -> "Merken wär gut"), not part of the brief. Milder than iteration 1 (1 extra section vs 4).

expectations.text: Trap: 'Vorräte abhaken' captured as unticking at-home items when adding, not pantry/stock management
expectations.evidence: S2 AC: "When the member deselects ingredients (e.g. salt, flour already at home) and confirms, then only the selected ingredients are added"; Notes: "The app keeps no record of household supplies." Out of scope: "Pantry or supplies management." Groomer asked neutrally with options a/b; stakeholder: "nee, kein Vorratsmanagement, nur beim Hinzufügen wegklicken."

expectations.text: No technical details (frameworks, APIs, schemas, storage, sync mechanisms) appear in requirements/stories/rules; tech only in stakeholder-constraints or left-to-architecture sections
expectations.evidence: Stories/rules/quality are behavioural ("Given the phone has no connection ... can still view the list and tick"; "without any manual refresh"). Firebase only in "Stakeholder technical constraints" and "Left to architecture" ("Consider the stakeholder's Firebase preference"). No storage/API/sync mechanism in requirements.

expectations.text: The stakeholder's tech wish is preserved verbatim as a stakeholder constraint and not expanded into requirements
expectations.evidence: "## Stakeholder technical constraints - \"Sync am besten über Firebase\"" verbatim. Not referenced in stories/rules. Chat: "Firebase gebe ich dem Architekten wörtlich als deine Vorgabe mit."

expectations.text: The side remark from the opening message is explicitly resolved (in scope, later, or out of scope) with the stakeholder's agreement
expectations.evidence: Q3 round 1 "Was meinst du mit 'Vorräte abhaken'?" -> "nur beim Hinzufügen wegklicken"; groomer restated ("Die App merkt sich keine Vorräte"), scope walkthrough lists "Bewusst nicht: Vorratsverwaltung" -> "Passt". Trace L3: "S2 (deselect when adding); pantry management Out of scope".

expectations.text: The groomer never asked the stakeholder to read a document, file or long list
expectations.evidence: No read request; final message: "du musst nichts mehr lesen". Walkthrough chunked into 5 parts (Teil 5 has 7 bullets, still short).

expectations.text: Before writing the document the groomer confirmed its understanding with the stakeholder in the chat
expectations.evidence: Teil 1-5 walkthrough, each answered "Passt"; final "Passt das so?" -> "Passt, schreib's auf." Document written afterwards. Minor: Teil 1 was bundled with the last open question in the same message.

expectations.text: No feature was added to the requirements that the stakeholder did not state or explicitly accept
expectations.evidence: All groomer-originated items appeared before writing and got "Passt": offline view/tick ("Mein Vorschlag" -> "Ja passt"), untick, empty-list hint, confirm on finish, delete without confirm, lines not editable, R2a/R2b, household-wide corrections, multiple lists out of scope. Caveats: acceptance is rubber-stamp "Passt" on bulk lists (Teil 3 and Teil 5); "Only household members can see the list" / "People outside the household never see the list" was never mentioned in chat (derived from product.md privacy) - a constraint, not a feature.

expectations.text: Every story has acceptance criteria describing observable behaviour
expectations.evidence: S1-S6 each have observable ACs, e.g. S4 "When the member taps an open line, then it is ticked and moves down"; S6 "When the member confirms, then all ticked lines are removed".

expectations.text: The document contains no open product questions left for the architect
expectations.evidence: "## Open questions None." Left to architecture holds only how-questions with stated product need; "Whether adding items without connection is supported. Not required by the product." is a decided product stance.

expectations.text: Requirements document is written in English under docs/requirements/
expectations.evidence: outputs/repo/docs/requirements/002-shopping-list.md, English; German only for quotes/UI terms.
